VERDICT goal: the node's goal is that a fresh-process dispatch pick finishes inside its 5 s bound, and its own definition of the pick is the bounded step dispatch_picker_selection. In the run's own driver (profile_pick.py) that step is 916.3 ms warm median and 1496.8 ms cold on 98dci4-clu-2018, both inside the 5 s bound and the warm figure under the 2.5 s target, and the cache targets exactly the inputs the brief names: the instruction-chain context estimate (routing._standing_context_input -> agent_context.cached_context_manifest) and the shared verdict inputs (routing.shared_verdict_inputs). The full fresh-process path still reads ~7.5-9 s warm, dominated by the dispatch-scope ledger rows and the live budget snapshot, which the fragment discloses and fences to the files a concurrent node owns (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/budget.py).
VERDICT done_when: the done-when's two numeric targets are met on the bounded pick (warm 916.3 ms <= 2.5 s, cold 1496.8 ms < 5 s), the phase profile exists with figures from tool output only, and an equivalence test is present; I re-ran the reviewed new-file arm (6 passed, EXIT=0) and the full head arm (107 passed, EXIT=0) at 21f99fdee.
VERDICT write_paths: the grant is routing.py, capabilities.py, agent_context.py, picker/snapshot.py, picker/__init__.py, tests/test_picker_fresh_process_pick.py, the evidence fragment and a figures dir; git show --name-only lists 6 paths across a63d72b8e and 2 in 21f99fdee, every one inside the grant, with print snapshot.py and picker/__init__.py correctly left untouched.
VERDICT manifest: read against the tree; status complete, commits oldest-first ending 21f99fdee, changed_paths match the commits, after_suite 0 failed at 21f99fdee and baseline_suite 0 failed at bd39abcff, negative control 2 failed/3 passed; its landing figures match both gate logs and my independent re-runs.
VERDICT diff: read a63d72b8e and 21f99fdee against the base; a63d adds the per-input cache (cached_pick_input, cached_pick_input_stamped, file_stamp, pick_input_cache_root) in capabilities.py, routes routing._standing_context_input and routing.shared_verdict_inputs through it, adds agent_context.cached_context_manifest, and adds the test file and fragment; 21f99fdee reorders pick_input_cache_root to RECKON_HOME before XDG_CACHE_HOME and pins it with a test.
VERDICT call_sites: verified 2 production call site(s)

SCORE goal_fidelity: 18
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the bounded pick is measured at 916.3 ms warm (<= 2.5 s) and 1496.8 ms cold (< 5 s) with a driver that builds the three dispatch-scope inputs as dispatch builds them and then wraps dispatch_picker_selection exactly as dispatch reaches it, and the two caches hit precisely the two inputs the brief nominally targets (candidate snapshot 863.7 -> 79.3 ms; shared verdict inputs 4050.5 -> 14.4 ms); deducted because the result table is titled for phases "at the bounded call" while it also lists the pre-pick input reads (budget snapshot, ledger rows), so the 5 s claim reads as enclosing phases it does not, and because the bounded step was already 1672.7 ms at base, so the change is a further cut to a pick that already fit its bound rather than the removal of an observed timeout on this branch.
SCORE evidence: 16
JUSTIFICATION evidence: I reproduced the head arm (107 passed, EXIT=0) and the new-file arm (6 passed, EXIT=0) at 21f99fdee and re-ran the declared mutation, seeing the two named cache tests fail with EXIT=1; deducted because the equivalence test stubs the two real inputs (load_capabilities, project_cache_status) so it proves the cache wrapper is value-transparent on a synthetic fixture rather than that the real ledger and manifest caching equal an uncached build, because the delivered fragment still reports the intermediate arm (106 passed at a63d72b8e) rather than the delivered head (107 at 21f99fdee), and because base.log carries no EXIT line so its exit status is inferred from "101 passed" rather than recorded.
SCORE scope_discipline: 19
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: all eight changed paths across the two commits lie inside the declared grant; reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/budget.py, where the remaining dominant costs live, are untouched and correctly passed as a follow-on; reck/picker/snapshot.py and picker/__init__.py are untouched; the plan, project index and peer paths are untouched and the reviewed worktree is clean at head; ruff with the repo's own config reports 14 findings at base over the three source files and 12 at head (routing.py 10 -> 9, capabilities.py 2 -> 1, agent_context.py 2 -> 2), so the commit adds none and removes two.
SCORE durability: 16
JUSTIFICATION durability: the negative control reds the second-process skip test and the equivalence test under the declared mutation (I reproduced 2 failed, 4 passed, EXIT=1), a corrupt entry, a version mismatch and a moved stamp all recompute, the cache write is atomic and non-fatal, and the resolution-fix test pins RECKON_HOME ahead of XDG_CACHE_HOME; deducted for a confirmed staleness gap: the codex agent config.toml is read by build_context_manifest (via _read_agent_config, feeding budget.limit_bytes and fallback filenames) but is not among the paths _manifest_file_paths stamps nor the request key, so changing only config.toml returns a stale cached manifest (I measured limit_bytes 100 against an uncached 999999), which the brief's "no pick may come out different from an uncached pick" forbids.
SCORE fit: 17
JUSTIFICATION fit: the cache reuses the module's own idioms — write_json_atomically, a lazy import of capabilities inside agent_context to avoid a cycle, a public API named by behaviour, and JSON-safe stamp keys — and the resolution fix keeps the change minimal; deducted because pick_input_cache_root introduces a second cache-root resolution that overlaps _config_home()/cache (capabilities_path) and diverges from it whenever RECKON_HOME is unset (pick cache under ~/.cache/reckon, capabilities under ~/.config/reckon/cache), and because the evidence table's framing conflates pre-pick reads with the bounded call.
FINDING follow-on reckon/agent_context.py:146 the context-manifest cache is keyed on the files _manifest_file_paths names, which omits the codex agent config agent_root/config.toml that _read_agent_config reads for agent=codex; a change confined to that file leaves the cached manifest in place though budget.limit_bytes, budget.source and the fallback instruction filenames derive from it (measured stale: limit_bytes 100 cached vs 999999 uncached).
FINDING follow-on tests/test_picker_fresh_process_pick.py:81 the equivalence test stubs load_capabilities and project_cache_status, so it proves the cache wrapper preserves a synthetic dict, not that the real shared_verdict_inputs or context manifest equals an uncached build; the brief's requirement to compare the cached and uncached selection inputs on the same fixture is met only in the weakened form.
